description: The bar chart illustrates the GPU memory usage (in GB) for various fine-tuning methods applied to language models across multiple datasets, as presented in the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical axis represents GPU Memory in gigabytes, ranging from 0 to approximately 70 GB, with tick marks at 0, 20, 40, and 60. The horizontal axis lists six methods: Full FT, MTL-FT, TAG, LoRA, QLoRA, and Ours, with labels rotated diagonally for readability. All bars except “Ours” are colored orange; “Ours” is green, visually distinguishing it as the proposed method. Full FT consumes the most memory at approximately 70 GB, followed by MTL-FT at around 40 GB. TAG and LoRA both use about 22 GB, while QLoRA uses the least among the orange bars at approximately 13 GB. The “Ours” method uses about 22 GB, comparable to TAG and LoRA but significantly less than Full FT and MTL-FT, highlighting its memory efficiency. A gray rectangular annotation is placed above the chart near the top, likely indicating a reference or threshold, though its specific meaning is not labeled. The bars are not sorted by value, but rather by method type, with “Ours” placed last to emphasize its performance relative to baselines.
